name: Adam Scaife
role: Head of Long-Range Forecasting, UK Met Office

name: Ken Graham
quote: Every El Nino is not the same; each one is unique with its own imprint on our weather.

name: Celeste Saulo
quote: We need to prepare for a potentially strong El Niño event – which will exacerbate drought and heavy rainfall and increase the risk of heatwaves both on land and in the ocean.

name: Leon Hermanson
role: Lead Author, WMO Global Annual to Decadal Climate Update
quote: The prediction of El Niño for the second half of 2026 increases the chances of the following year, 2027, being the next record-breaking year.

name: Frederike Otto
role: Climate Scientist, World Weather Attribution / Imperial College London
quote: Climate change will likely play a larger role in extreme weather events than El Niño will.

name: NOAA Climate Prediction Center

name: Peru Ministry of Production (PRODUCE)
quote: Anchovy fishing in the North-Central zone remains suspended as warm coastal waters continue to disperse the stock.

name: BMKG (Indonesia Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency)
quote: The 2026 dry season will be more intense and prolonged than usual, with a higher risk of wildfires and drought due in part to El Niño.

name: Kenya Meteorological Department

name: Panama Canal Authority

name: Munich Re

name: WisdomTree Commodity Strategists

name: Jessica Luna
quote: It's a devastating blow to the sector. We usually create 250,000 jobs — 122,000 will be lost by next year.

name: Douglas Uggah Embas
quote: Any area whose Air Pollutant Index crosses 500 will face emergency closure of non-essential services.

name: Jundy del Socorro
role: Chief, DENR Environmental Management Bureau, Philippines

name: Celeste Saulo

name: António Guterres

name: Wisdom Kofi Dogbey
role: Managing Director, Cocoa Marketing Company Ghana Ltd.
quote: We have structural problems in Ghana. Trees are old and we still have issues with diseases. We also have pollination that is failing for various reasons — we haven't seen that in 20 years.

name: Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD)
quote: 2026/27 cocoa production could fall to 450,000-550,000 tonnes from 750,000 tonnes projected for 2025/26, due to the combined effects of swollen shoot disease, aging farms, and the likelihood of adverse weather from the El Niño pattern.
